prompt:
Repair the WALKING ANATOMY in the attached original ASHVEIL cinder-bear walk atlas; keep this same original bear identity, precise detailed pixel-art style, charcoal/soot-brown ash-tipped fur, small round ears, broad short muzzle, massive shoulder hump/rump and four stout natural bear legs. The previous sheet did not alternate the visible foreleg clearly enough. Draw NEW correct walking poses, not a recolor or simple translation of the same planted foreleg.

Exactly FOUR ROWS x FOUR COLUMNS, 16 fully separated complete sprites on true transparent RGBA. Row1 FRONT toward bottom; row2 LEFT, nose left; row3 RIGHT, nose right; row4 BACK toward top, rump nearest viewer. Do not mix directions within a row. Same elevated three-quarter camera/head size/body mass. No shadows/floor/grid/labels/text/checkerboard/effects. VERY LARGE transparent gutters: every silhouette entirely in the center 55 percent of its cell, leave one full bear-paw width clear on each side, never touch canvas edges or neighbors.

CRITICAL FOUR POSES, each row from column1 to4: (1) NEAR foreleg stretches forward, NEAR forepaw plants ahead; FAR foreleg is behind. (2) NEAR forepaw now supports weight UNDER shoulder, FAR forepaw clearly LIFTS with bent elbow preparing forward. (3) FAR foreleg now stretches forward with FAR forepaw ahead; NEAR foreleg is swept BACK/under shoulder and MUST NOT again stretch forward. (4) NEAR forepaw clearly LIFTS off the ground with bent elbow, FAR forepaw supports weight under shoulder. Alternate hind paws as well, a slow heavy four-beat walk with at least two/three support paws, never a flying trot. Show both forelegs separately wherever not naturally occluded; do not invent fifth legs. Column3 and4 MUST differ from1 and2 in which forepaw is ahead/lifted. Front row visibly alternates viewer-left and viewer-right front paws, back row alternates rear paws. Keep strong shoulder weight, compact stable body, gentle body bob. This is four-legged locomotion, never upright/humanoid, no attack paws.
